title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1970-02-08

ai_review.summary: A strong 1970 San Francisco show with a smoking Smokestack Lightning opener and epic Lovelight, captured on a mixed SBD/Audience composite that is decent but not pristine.
ai_review.review: The performance shines – the band rolls out one of the best Smokestack Lightning openers, rare gems like Sitting On Top of the World, a soaring Dark Star and a marathon Love Light that many reviewers call legendary. The recording is a matrix‑type composite; it sounds better than average with clear audience ambience, though drums sit low, the mix can be tinny or phased and some sections are unbalanced.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the musical performance (many 4‑5★) while noting only moderate recording flaws, resulting in a high overall score weighted toward show quality.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Better than average mix; audience source is solid, drums are a bit low, occasional tinny/phased character and balance issues in the composite. Some sections (Morning Dew, Dire Wolf) suffer from poor source quality.

standout_songs: Sitting On Top of the World
China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
St. Stephen > Not Fade Away > St. Stephen
show_quality.setlist_flow: A powerful opener with Smokestack, followed by rare early‑’70 material and a seamless sandwich of St. Stephen/Not Fade/Away, culminating in an expansive 35‑minute Love Light that caps the night.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia's guitar tone is repeatedly praised – chiming on China Cat, back‑and‑forth with Pigpen during Lovelight, and strong interplay with Bob.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s rhythm work and vocal harmonies are highlighted, especially his interplay with Garcia in the SBD sections.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen's organ rap on Lovelight is called out as a highlight; no specific comments about Keith/Brent/Vince.
band_member_comments.Drums: Drums are noted as being low in the mix.
